reach.rationale: Every runtime framework API (Hono v4, @hono/node-server v2, hono/jsx async components, htmx 2.x) is long-stable; the sole recently-stable element is TypeScript 7, a stable but ~3-month-old major rewrite that powers the build step.

evidence: app/src/index.tsx:26-33 — the only adapter-specific config (serveStatic) sits behind one /static/* route
app/public/app.js:1-36 — all client interactivity is one plain DOM script, trivially replaceable
app/src/api.ts:18-47 — caching/concurrency is a hand-rolled Map/semaphore, no preview runtime features

containment.rationale: There is essentially nothing experimental to contain; the few newer surfaces (htmx attributes, serveStatic options, TS 7) each sit behind a single module or one route, so any of them could be swapped in isolation.

evidence: app/package.json:9-10 — stays on Hono 4 stable and htmx 2.x stable instead of Hono v5 RC or the unshipped htmx 4.0 line
app/src/index.tsx:37-43 — HX-Push-Url is the correct htmx 2.x header name (not the deprecated 1.x X-Push-Url), i.e. current idioms, not novelty
app/scripts/copy-assets.mjs:8-10 — ships htmx from node_modules with plain fs, no build-tool beta features
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all; the choices are deliberately conservative and current (latest stable versions of stable majors), so there is nothing gratuitous or novelty-driven.

findings.issue: TypeScript ^7.0.2 (the Go-native rewrite) was released only ~3 months ago; it is the official stable 'latest' but editor plug-ins and team tooling across an org may still lag, and a floating ^7 range will silently pick up the young 7.1 line.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep — it is stable — but consider confirming the team's editors/CI support TS 7 and pinning an exact version (7.0.2) rather than ^7 so builds don't move to a newer minor without intent.

findings.issue: Hono v5.0.0-rc.1 is already on npm; when it ships, this app will need a peer/adaptor bump to @hono/node-server.
findings.suggestion: No action needed now (using the stable v4 line is the right call); just note that the migration surface is small since the app touches only Hono/Context, hono/html, hono/jsx and serveStatic.

summary: The app is maximally conservative on experimentalness: zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs, with every dependency on the current stable release line (Hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.x, htmx.org 2.0.11). The only recently-stable piece is TypeScript 7.0.2 as the build compiler, which is a stable official release used with no experimental compiler flags. Risk of breaking changes from upstream is negligible.
